ordered_diagnoses: Congenital heart disease with shunt reversal

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic exertional chest pain and shortness of breath with progressive cyanosis and lower extremity edema
salient_findings: Recurrent post-activity chest pain and shortness of breath for more than 11 years
Bilateral lower extremity edema for one week
Cyanosis developed after an episode of severe cough and hemoptysis in 2016
key_facts: Patient is a 39-year-old male
Symptoms began in 2010 with post-activity chest pain and shortness of breath
Patient was initially acyanotic from 2010 to 2016
Severe cough and hemoptysis episode in 2016 led to cyanosis
Femoral artery oxygen saturation decreased from 93.4% in 2016 to 88.5%
Plasma N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide was 94.2 pg/ml in August 2021
Chest CT showed enlarged hilar shadow and widened pulmonary arteries
Echocardiography revealed markedly enlarged right atrium and right ventricle with tricuspid regurgitation
Estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure was 55 mmHg in 2021
Right Heart Catheterization showed pulmonary artery pressure of 60/39 mmHg
Transesophageal Echocardiography revealed a patent foramen ovale with a continuous right-to-left shunt

shortlist: Congenital heart disease with shunt reversal

shortlist.label: Eisenmenger syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has chronic exertional chest pain, shortness of breath, and progressive cyanosis, with evidence of right-to-left shunt on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Congenital heart disease with shunt reversal
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a patent foramen ovale with a continuous right-to-left shunt, suggesting a congenital heart defect with shunt reversal

shortlist.label: Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has elevated pulmonary artery systolic pressure and tricuspid regurgitation, with no clear cause for pulmonary hypertension

shortlist.label: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of hemoptysis and pulmonary embolism is a possible cause of pulmonary hypertension

shortlist.label: Tricuspid regurgitation due to endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has tricuspid regurgitation and a history of severe cough and hemoptysis, which could be related to endocarditis

raw.rationale: The patient's long history of post-activity chest pain and shortness of breath, progression from acyanotic to cyanotic, decreased femoral artery oxygen saturation, and imaging findings of enlarged right atrium and ventricle with tricuspid regurgitation and a patent foramen ovale with right-to-left shunt are consistent with Eisenmenger syndrome, a condition characterized by a congenital heart defect with reversed shunt due to pulmonary hypertension.

rejected.label: Congenital heart disease with shunt reversal
rejected.why: While the patient has a congenital heart defect, the specific diagnosis of Eisenmenger syndrome better explains the combination of pulmonary hypertension, right heart enlargement, and cyanosis.

rejected.label: Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension
rejected.why: The presence of a patent foramen ovale and the patient's history suggest a congenital component rather than idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension.

rejected.label: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
rejected.why: Pulmonary angiography showed no evidence of pulmonary embolism or arteriovenous fistulae, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Tricuspid regurgitation due to endocarditis
rejected.why: There is no mention of endocarditis in the patient's history, and the tricuspid regurgitation is more likely secondary to the pulmonary hypertension and right heart enlargement.

gold: Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (IPAH) with Patent Foramen Ovale (PFO)
